DESCRIPTION: FIND — resume mode cannot reliably resume the latest run because `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` looks for `checkpoint.json`, while this runner persists its own state to `runner_state.json` and later resume logic reads `runner_state.json` plus `brain.load_checkpoint()`. Premises: (1) `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` under `if cfg.resume:` returns the first log dir where `(c / "checkpoint.json").exists()`. (2) This file writes runner state to `runner_state.json` every round. (3) HIL pause path calls `brain._save_checkpoint()`, which may create `checkpoint.json`, but ordinary runs and crashes between `brain.persist()`/runner-state writes are only guaranteed to have `runner_state.json`. Concrete trace: create `bench/logs/ref_x_20260413T000000Z/runner_state.json` with valid registry state, but no `checkpoint.json`; start with `--resume`. `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` finds no matching checkpoint, creates a fresh timestamped directory, then `brain.load_checkpoint()` runs in the new directory and resume silently starts from round 0. Expected: resume should pick the existing run with persisted state. Actual: it can fork a new run and lose continuity. Formal conclusion: the resume directory selector is keyed to the wrong checkpoint artifact and can silently break resumability, which is a high-severity correctness fault in a long-running experiment runner.
FOLLOW: This crosses the CLI `--resume` interface, log directory selection, checkpoint restoration, HIL workflow, and burst-state/ITC restoration. Downstream effects: duplicated experiment directories, lost registry continuity, wrong `start_round`, missing burst_state restoration, stale fingerprint/ITC histories, and potentially inconsistent operator expectations after exit code 42. Because convergence and HIL gates depend on restored histories, a failed resume corrupts experiment semantics rather than merely UI state.

(3) At the “All phases done — start integration round” branch, it clears the same histories but omits resetting `consecutive_churn_rounds`. (4) Integration convergence checks call `_check_stall_convergence(..., consecutive_churn_rounds=consecutive_churn_rounds)` and also use the separate churn transition path. Concrete trace: last phase ends with `consecutive_churn_rounds = 3` and `gamma >= 0.45`; integration starts; histories are empty but churn counter remains 3. On the first integration round, if rho_churn remains true once, counter becomes 4 and `_check_stall_convergence` can emit `STALL_CONVERGED (churn)` immediately, even though integration has only seen one round. Expected: integration should start with fresh convergence state. Actual: stale churn state leaks across phases. Formal conclusion: this is a confirmed state-leak bug that can cause premature integration termination.
FOLLOW: This affects burst-mode only, but it directly impacts convergence, HIL pause points, report correctness (`convergence_reason`), and operator trust in burst decomposition. DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_experiment()` computes cumulative context telemetry from response lengths instead of prompt/context lengths, so endocrine context-budget monitoring is measuring output volume, not actual context pressure. (3) Yet after dispatch, the loop does `for label, text in responses.items(): per_model_context[label] += len(text); cumulative_context_chars += len(text)`. (4) `endo.run(... cumulative_context_chars=cumulative_context_chars, context_budget=max(CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET.values()), ...)` consumes this metric. Concrete trace: suppose five models each receive 80k-char prompts and answer with 2k chars. Real context pressure is ~400k chars sent; recorded `cumulative_context_chars` is only ~10k. Expected endocrine pacing should detect heavy prompt pressure. Actual telemetry underreports by ~40x and can suppress pacing/health signals. Formal conclusion: this is a confirmed correctness bug in the monitoring path; it silently corrupts the control signal used for pacing.
FOLLOW: This crosses dispatch, endocrine pacing, round telemetry, and any downstream adaptive logic keyed off `cumulative_context_chars`. It does not break dispatch itself, but it undermines the feedback loop meant to prevent context overload. That is high impact because the same runner has elaborate fingerprint/budget logic whose observability is then fed bad data.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — HIL review in burst mode can re-pause forever at the same phase boundary because the pause path exits before marking any “already paused/reviewed” progress in `burst_state`, and the resume path restores `burst_state` unchanged. Premises: (1) In burst convergence handling, when `cfg.hil_review` is true, the code writes a partial report and `sys.exit(42)` before advancing `phase_idx`, `integration_started`, `phase_round_offset`, or resetting convergence state. (2) `runner_state.json` persists `burst_state`. (3) On resume, `_restored_burst` is loaded verbatim. (4) The same round/phase convergence condition remains true, so execution re-enters the same HIL gate and exits 42 again. Concrete trace: phase 0 converges; burst HIL gate writes report and exits. Resume restores `burst_state["phase_idx"] == 0`, current registry/histories still at converged boundary, then re-executes the same branch and exits again before transition to phase 1. Expected: one pause per boundary, then resume should advance. Actual: operator can get stuck in an infinite review loop. Formal conclusion: confirmed control-flow bug in the burst HIL path.
FOLLOW: This affects collaborative review workflow, makes `--resume --hil-review` unusable in burst mode, and blocks progress on large targets. It also causes duplicate partial reports and repeated exit code 42 without state advancement.
